 by

 Following a cold, cloudy, blustery few days, a warmer, drier, and sunnier weather pattern is expected to take hold from Tuesday through the weekend. High temperatures will be running 15 degrees above normal for much of the week, though with clear skies and light winds, temps will cool off to near-freezing overnight. No major weather issues are anticipated for Tompkins County in the week ahead.

 Your Weekly Weather
 Following the late-week storm system that impacted much of the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic, a large area of clockwise-spinning high pressure is moving in from the west. Widespread cool air flow from the NW is resulting in near-overcast skies and cellular instability rain showers across much of the Finger Lakes and Southern Tier, enhanced by the warm water destabilizing the cold air passing overhead. However, the angle is catching the lake on its short axis, so there is limited energy transfer.
 As the winds weaken through the evening and into the overnight hours, the showers will end, but the clouds will stubbornly persist. High pressure will move over the Ohio River Valley and into the Mid-Atlantic through the first half of the week. The drier, more stable air of the high will begin to break down the cloud sheet later tomorrow. 
 For the remainder of your Sunday, expect a cold northwest wind and near-overcast skies with a few light rain showers. Highs will be below normal, in the lower 40s. Tonight will not see temps recede much given the clouds, though showers should taper off. Lows will be in the mid to upper 30s.
 Monday will be a little warmer as the northwest wind weakens. Expect cloudy skies to start the day, with some partial clearing towards sunset. Highs will be in the mid 40s. Monday night will become mostly clear with calm air, allowing for a colder night with lows around 30.
 By Tuesday, the clockwise-spinning high over the Mid-Atlantic allows us to receive winds from the southwest, and those winds will allow temperatures to rebound to above-normal values for mid-November. A dry, mostly sunny day is on tap for Tompkins County, with highs in the upper 50s. Tuesday night will be dry and mostly clear with lows in the lower 30s.
 The high stays largely in place for Wednesday and Thursday. Calm air and near-clear skies will allow for a mild November day Wednesday, with highs around 60. Wednesday night will see a few passing clouds with lows in the lower 30s.
 Thursday will be fairly similar, maybe even a touch warmer as a system to the northwest enhances the northwest flank of the high’s flow. Expect mostly sunny skies for the Ithaca area, with highs in the low 60s. Thursday night will be partly cloudy and milder with lows in the low 40s.
 Current model projections show the storm staying well to the north of Tompkins County Friday. This will allow for another mild, dry day, with partly cloudy skies and highs in the low 60s. Friday night is expected to be partly cloudy with lows around 40.
 Looking ahead into next weekend, it’s rather like a game of storm system dodgeball. Two storm systems are expected to develop, one that moves northeast and then east across the Upper Midwest and Canada, the other moving northeast from the U.S. Southeast to the Mid-Atlantic Coast. The primary forecast models show both systems missing Tompkins County, at least through the weekend, though some more seasonably cool air is likely to briefly return early the following week. For now, plan for dry weather and a mix of sun clouds for both Saturday and Sunday, with highs in the low 60s Saturday and around 60 Sunday, and lows in the low 40s and upper 30s respectively.
 Graphics courtesy of the NOAA Climate Prediction Center 
 Extended Outlook
 Looking ahead into the Thanksgiving travel week, the large-scale weather pattern favors a return to above normal temperatures after a short cool spell, with a jet stream ridge likely to result in high temps in the 50s and 60s across much of the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic, when typical values are in the mid 40s. 
 However, it also looks like this would drive Atlantic coastal systems on a more northward track, allowing for more abundant rain during the holiday travel period. However, this is not likely to be a major travel issue regionally, and there’s little chance of snow during the forecast period. So if you’ll be on the road or receiving travelers for Thanksgiving, you can be cautiously optimistic that the weather won’t be an issue in this corner of the country.
